topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the cancer biology lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Cancer development and the disruption of normal tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as altered cellular behaviour within organised tissues, whose context must be preserved to understand the disease.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumours through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how invasion and spread distinguish malignancy from contained benign growth, using clinical and histological evidence.

topics.label: Tumour progression and the malignant potential of benign growths
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine progression from benign growth to invasive cancer while showing that neither malignant transformation nor safety is guaranteed by a benign diagnosis.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and ultimately causes morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumour types across populations and species to show how widely cancer arises.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why early detection is needed and how the effectiveness of screening depends on the cancer being screened.

topics.label: Lecture close and preparation for revision and practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This closing directs students back to the learning outcomes and signals the upcoming practicals and lecture.
